documents.title: Psychiatry progress letter
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
OUTPATIENT PSYCHIATRY — LETTER TO PRIMARY CARE
Date of visit: 10/07/2020

Dear colleague,

I saw Ms. Brooks, 42, for her scheduled follow-up of bipolar disorder. She has remained stable on lithium
throughout the past two years, takes it reliably, and reports no manic or depressive episodes. She had no
concerns of her own today, though on questioning she mentioned that she has been thirstier and urinating more
than usual over the last few weeks. Mental status and a brief physical examination were unremarkable.

Labs drawn here today:
  Sodium 142 mEq/L | Potassium 4.1 mEq/L | Creatinine 1.0 mg/dL | Calcium 10.2 mg/dL
  Lithium 1.2 mEq/L (therapeutic 0.6-1.2)
  TSH 5.5 uIU/mL (ref 0.4-4.0)

Impression: bipolar disorder, stable. Lithium-associated (drug-induced) hypothyroidism, mild, with a TSH just
above range.

Plan: continue lithium carbonate 300 mg twice daily. No thyroid replacement at this level; I would ask that you
repeat a TSH with free T4 in 6 to 8 weeks along with her usual lithium level and renal panel. I will see her
again in 3 months.

Current medications: lithium carbonate 300 mg BID; sumatriptan 100 mg PRN. Allergies: NKDA.

Outpatient psychiatry

which lithium can do. Nothing to start now. We'll recheck it with your usual lithium labs in early December
and add a free T4. I scheduled you for Monday 12/7 at 7:30. Flu shot whenever you can come by.

documents.title: New medicine from rheumatology
documents.author: patient
documents.body:
Hi, my fingers were going white a lot more this winter so I called my rheumatologist last week and she started
me on amlodipine 5 mg on Friday. The finger attacks already seem better but I keep noticing my heartbeat when
I'm sitting at my desk and my face gets flushed. No chest pain, not dizzy. Is this normal? I see rheum on
Wednesday.

documents.title: RE: New medicine from rheumatology
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Thanks for letting me know - I've added amlodipine to your list here. Flushing and being more aware of your
heartbeat are common in the first couple of weeks on amlodipine and often settle. Keep the Wednesday
appointment and ask them to send us a note. If you get chest pain, feel faint or lightheaded, or your heart
races and doesn't settle, call us right away or go to the ER.

documents.title: Rheumatology follow-up letter
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
RHEUMATOLOGY — FOLLOW-UP NOTE (received by fax 06/07/2021)
Date of service: 04/14/2021

Patient: Erin Brooks, 42-year-old woman with bipolar disorder on lithium and long-standing Raynaud
phenomenon, seen in continuing follow-up.

Interval: After a winter of more frequent vasospastic attacks she called us, and amlodipine 5 mg daily was
started by phone on 04/09. Five days in, she already has fewer attacks. She has noticed her heartbeat even at
rest and occasional facial flushing. No chest pain, dizziness or leg swelling. Migraine history noted; no recent
attack.

Medications: lithium carbonate 300 mg BID, sumatriptan 100 mg PRN (max 200 mg/day), amlodipine 5 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: Vital signs stable. Heart without murmur, rub or gallop. Lungs clear without crackles or wheeze.
Extremities warm, peripheral pulses good, capillary refill brisk, no edema.

ECG (baseline, today): normal.

Assessment: Chronic vasospastic disorder — her Raynaud phenomenon — improving on a dihydropyridine calcium
channel blocker. Palpitations and flushing are expected effects of this class and do not warrant stopping.

Plan: continue amlodipine 5 mg daily. Cold protection as before. Return in 12 months or sooner if attacks
worsen or digital ulcers appear.

Rheumatology

Annual physical, 42F.

Since last year: rheumatology started amlodipine 5 mg in April for a rough Raynaud winter. Their note came in
last week. Fingers much better; the flushing and heartbeat awareness wore off after about two weeks. TSH was
mildly high last fall on lithium (psychiatry letter, 5.5); December recheck still mildly high with normal free
T4, being watched. Psychiatry every 3 months, mood steady. Migraines 2/month. COVID vaccines done at a pharmacy
in April and May.

Meds: lithium carbonate 300 mg BID (psychiatry); amlodipine 5 mg daily (rheumatology); sumatriptan 100 mg PRN.
NKDA.

Exam: comfortable. Thyroid normal size, no nodules, nontender. RRR without murmur. Lungs clear. Breast exam
normal bilaterally. Abdomen benign. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix normal; Pap/HPV collected.
Hands warm, pink, no ulcers. No edema.

PHQ-9 2.

Plan
1. Bipolar d/o: lithium level, BMP today, to psychiatry.
2. Subclinical hypothyroidism on lithium: TSH + FT4 today.
3. Raynaud: improved on amlodipine, rheum following.
4. Migraine: unchanged, refilled.
5. HM: Pap/HPV today. CBC. COVID series entered from state registry. Mammogram 2022. Flu in fall.

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit, pt at her desk at work, identity confirmed.

CC: loose stools.

HPI: About 9 days of watery stools, 4-5 a day. No blood, no mucus. No belly pain to speak of, no fever, no
vomiting. Eating normally. Hasn't traveled; nobody at home or work sick. Drinking plenty. Hasn't changed what
she eats. No antibiotics.

On lithium, so my main concern is volume and her level.

Meds: lithium carbonate 300 mg BID, amlodipine 5 mg daily, sumatriptan PRN. NKDA.

Exam (video): well-appearing, not ill, mucous membranes look moist, speaking full sentences.

A/P: Persistent watery diarrhea, 9 days, no red flags.
- Lithium level and BMP this afternoon at our lab.
- She would like to be seen by GI since it is going on this long; referral placed, GI has an opening Monday.
- Fluids; call if fever, blood, lightheadedness, tremor, confusion, or unsteady walking (signs of a high
  lithium level).

documents.title: Gastroenterology consultation
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
GASTROENTEROLOGY CONSULTATION
Date of service: 04/18/2022
Referred by: primary care

Reason: two weeks of loose stools.

History: Ms. Brooks is a 43-year-old woman with bipolar disorder, migraine and Raynaud phenomenon. She reports
two weeks of 4 to 5 watery bowel movements a day, without blood or mucus. No abdominal pain, weight loss,
travel, sick contacts, known food allergies or change in diet. When asked specifically about supplements, she
told us that about three weeks ago, after reading about natural treatments for migraine, she started a
magnesium oxide 400 mg capsule each night at bedtime.

Medications: lithium carbonate 300 mg BID; sumatriptan 100 mg PRN (max 200 mg/day); amlodipine 5 mg daily.
Supplement: magnesium oxide 400 mg at bedtime (self-started).
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: never smoker, no alcohol, administrative assistant.

Exam: vital signs within normal limits. Abdomen soft and nontender, bowel sounds increased. No masses.

Studies: CBC, electrolytes and TSH normal. Stool culture, ova and parasites and fecal leukocytes negative.

Impression: osmotic diarrhea from magnesium oxide.

Plan: stop the magnesium oxide; stools should normalize within days. Colonoscopy is not indicated at her age
without red flags. Please contact us if diarrhea persists beyond two weeks off magnesium.

Gastroenterology

documents.title: GI consult reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
GI letter reviewed. Diarrhea attributed to self-started magnesium oxide, advised to stop; stool studies
negative. I didn't ask about supplements at the video visit. Added to list as stopped supplement; will
message pt to confirm she's better.

documents.title: GI letter
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Erin, the GI note came in. They think the magnesium was the cause. How are things since you stopped it?

documents.title: RE: GI letter
documents.author: patient
documents.body:
I stopped it the night of the appointment and was back to normal in like 3 days. Lesson learned on internet
remedies! Thank you.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
PREVENTIVE VISIT

Erin is here for her yearly. Diarrhea in April turned out to be the magnesium she had started on her own for
migraine; resolved within days of stopping. GI did not want a colonoscopy at 43. Mood stable, psych every 3
months. Raynaud much better on amlodipine this past winter. Migraines 1-3/month on sumatriptan.

Meds: lithium carbonate 300 mg BID; amlodipine 5 mg daily; sumatriptan 100 mg PRN. No supplements now.
NKDA.

Exam: no distress. Thyroid normal. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Breast exam normal. Abdomen soft, nontender,
normal bowel sounds. No edema. Fingers warm.

PHQ-9 3.

Assessment/plan
- Bipolar disorder on lithium: level, CMP, TSH today; copy to psychiatry.
- TSH: back in range at GI in April. Recheck today; if normal again, will take lithium-related
  hypothyroidism off the active list. Either way it stays on the 6-month lithium panel.
- Raynaud: continue amlodipine.
- Migraine: stable. Advised to run supplements by us first.
- HM: lipids, CBC. Mammogram this fall (ordered). Colon cancer screening starts at 45 — next year. Flu and
  COVID booster in the fall.
